hints: For each x<=10^6, count its divisors by counting how many primes divide it and their exponents.
A sieve can build the smallest prime factor for every number.
For x=p^e times other factors, its divisor count multiplies by e+1 for each prime factor.
analogy: Each divisor independently chooses an exponent from zero through the exponent in x.
algorithm: Build smallest-prime-factor values with a sieve. Factor each query x by repeated division and multiply (exponent+1) for each prime.
correctness: Every divisor chooses one allowed exponent for each prime factor, and these independent choices produce every divisor exactly once.
complexity: O(M log log M+q log M) preprocessing/query time and O(M) space, where M is the maximum bound.
